purpose: Teach: 完備/部局/蓄え/出向い/改築/仮設/通さ/まずまず

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 創業時、本気で、設備、完備、苦労したぞ、ばあさんの代から、お前にも、絶対、伝えたい、本気で、頼んだぞ、本当に。
lines.en: When we founded this company, we equipped it properly — but it cost us everything. Your grandmother lived through that struggle. I need you to understand that. Please. I'm asking you seriously.
lines.style: Quiet, patient weight to every word. Speaks as though from long memory. Pauses between phrases. No rush—the kind of deliberate tempo that makes you listen. Voice settles slightly at the end, like he's done what he came to do.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: はい。お父さんの代から、各部局、本気で、頑張ってくれて、社員、絶対、感謝、しております、本気で、本当に、絶対、本気。
lines.en: Yes. Since my father's time, every department has given their genuine effort. The staff—I'm truly grateful for that. Sincerely.
lines.style: Steady, measured acknowledgment. Speaks with composed respect toward the absent father. Each phrase lands cleanly. Slight formality in register—the politeness of a son honoring his father's legacy. Warm but structured.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 創業期、蓄え、本気で、なかった時代、覚えてる、お父さん?苦労したぞ、お前にも、絶対、伝えていきたい、本気で、絶対、本当に。
lines.en: Back in the founding days, we had almost nothing in reserves. Do you remember that, Dad? The struggle was real. I want to pass that understanding on to you. I'm serious. I really am.
lines.style: Softer than the first line, tinged with longing. As if retrieving a memory that still moves him. Slower pace on the middle questions. Slight breathiness before committing to the final assertion—the work of persuading and remembering at once.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: はい。お父さん、お得意様に、本気で、何度も、出向いた話、私、本気で、感謝、しております、本当に、絶対、お父さん、絶対。
lines.en: Yes. The story of how my father visited our best clients so many times, working so hard to maintain those relationships—I'm truly grateful for that. I really am grateful, Dad. Absolutely.
lines.style: Warm and sincere, with a slight catch of emotion beneath the formality. Speaks the father's name with quiet reverence. Steady pace but slightly fuller breath—the voice of someone honoring sacrifice he witnessed. Ends with quiet conviction.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 本社の改築、お父さんの代から、本気で、続けてきたぞ、絶対、お前にも、引き継いで欲しい、本気で、頼んだぞ、絶対、本気。
lines.en: The rebuilding of the headquarters—my father carried that work forward seriously. I need you to carry it forward too. I'm counting on you. Seriously.
lines.style: Clear directive tone, but not harsh. Speaks with the quiet authority of handing something precious forward. Emphasis on 'carried forward'—weight there. Slower final phrases. No question mark in the voice, even where grammar might invite one. This is legacy speaking.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: はい。創業期、仮設の社屋、お父さん、本気で、苦労したんですよね、本当に、絶対、感謝、しております、本気で、お父さん、絶対。
lines.en: Yes. When we were in those temporary offices during the founding days, my father struggled through that. I'm truly grateful for that sacrifice. Really, I am, Dad. Absolutely.
lines.style: Respectful and warm, with a note of recognition for what came before. Speaks his father's name with affection beneath the formality. Measured pace. Slight emphasis on 'struggled through'—honoring the weight of it. Closes with quiet certainty.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: お得意様、絶対、相手に、通さない厳しさ、本気で、お父さん、貫いてきたぞ、お前にも、絶対、教えたい、本気で、絶対、本気で。
lines.en: Our best clients—my father maintained a standard of strictness with them. He never compromised on that principle. Not once. I want to teach you that same discipline. Truly. I'm serious about that.
lines.style: More directive and firmer than previous lines, but still patient. Emphasis lands on 'never compromised.' Speaks with conviction about principle. Pauses before the final assertion—gathering intention. The voice of someone passing down non-negotiable values.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: はい。今期、まずまずの、成績、本気で、お父さんに、ご報告できる、絶対、嬉しいです、本気で、感謝、しております、絶対、お父さん、本当に。
lines.en: Yes. This quarter we have solid results—results I'm genuinely proud to report to you, Dad. That makes me happy. Truly happy. I'm grateful. Thank you, Dad. Really.
lines.style: Warmer closing. A note of quiet pride and relief underneath the formality. Slightly quicker pace—the buoyancy of good news being shared. Speaks the father's name with deep affection at the end. Final phrase trails with genuine warmth rather than obligation.
